sourceFlowReconstruction.content: Mishnah. Seven days before Yom Kippur the Kohen Gadol is separated from his house to the Parhedrin chamber, and another kohen is prepared in his place lest a disqualification befall him. R. Yehuda: another wife is prepared too, lest his wife die, since it says "he shall atone for himself and for his house" and "his house" is his wife. They said to him: if so, there is no end to the matter. No ruling is stated.

Gemara opens "tnan hatam": seven days before the burning of the parah the kohen who burns it was separated from his house to the chamber on the face of the Bira, north-east, called the Chamber of the Stone House. Why that name? Because all its (the parah's) acts were with dung, stone, and earth vessels.

What is the reason? Since a tevul yom is fit for the parah, as we learned (detnan): they would make the kohen who burns the parah tamei and immerse him, to remove [the view] from the heart of the Sadducees, who said it was done by those whose sun had set. So the Rabbis instituted dung, stone, and earth vessels, which do not receive tumah, so that people not treat it lightly.

Why north-east? Since it is a chatat and a chatat requires the north, and it is written of it "toward the front of the Tent of Meeting", the Rabbis instituted a chamber north-east so that it have a distinguishing sign (hekeira).

What is Bira? Rabba bar bar Chana in the name of R. Yochanan: a place on the Temple Mount named Bira. Reish Lakish: the whole Temple is called Bira, as it says "the Bira which I have prepared". No resolution.

Mena hanei milei? R. Minyomi bar Chilkiya, in the name of R. Machseya bar Idi, in the name of R. Yochanan: "As was done this day, the Lord commanded to do, to atone for you": "to do" is the acts of the parah, "to atone" is the acts of Yom Kippur. Challenge: granted the whole verse cannot be about the parah, since "to atone" is written and the parah is not a matter of atonement; but say the whole verse is about Yom Kippur? Answer (amri): learn tziva-tziva; here "tziva Hashem la'asot", there "zot chukat haTorah asher tziva Hashem lemor"; as there parah so here parah, and as here separation so there separation.

"Ve'eima" - a further objection begins and is cut off by the physical end of 2a. The derivation is therefore still under challenge at the end of the daf; nothing about its outcome may be stated as reached here.

defects.candidateSays: Quote Lev 8:34 as 'as He commanded to do, to atone' / 'As the Lord commanded to do, to atone'
defects.sourceSupports: Lines 29-30: 'ka'asher asa bayom hazeh tziva Hashem la'asot lechaper aleichem' = 'As was done this day, the Lord commanded to do, to atone for you'. 'Ka'asher' governs 'asa bayom hazeh', not 'tziva'. The quotation silently drops words and fuses the clause into a different sentence. The derash on 'to do'/'to atone' is unaffected. Low severity but a proof-text misquotation inside quotation marks.
